correctness.rationale: Finite exhaustive certificate: for each n=3,4, fixing first-agent ranking by unique house relabeling leaves (n!)^(n-1) canonical profiles with exactly n! labeled realizations. Every pair of assignments receives an integer weak-majority margin, transitive closure identifies exactly the top cycle, and an all-rivals strict Pareto test identifies PO. Complete independent C++ bitset closure and Python breadth-first search recalculate all 42 joint frequencies exactly; sums 216 and 331776 and independent hand counts for 31104 and 20736 agree. No general-n or computational impossibility claim.

value.rationale: In the smallest house-allocation market with the known exceptional top-cycle size, this natural complete two-statistic distribution quantifies the selectivity defect of an important majority-based correspondence: the top cycle returns all 24 assignments with probability 415/576, and with probability 1/18 it returns all 24 even though only three assignments are Pareto-efficient. Joint counts are not a routine formal restatement of the prior support theorem, supply an exact impartial-culture benchmark, and are structurally interpretable for mechanism evaluation. Limit: a finite small-market classification, not a general-size theorem.
